Direct Sale from Tanker Owner

Fuel bought from a supplier and sent straight to a customer - it never enters this pump's tanks and never goes through a nozzle. Nothing here touches tank stock or litres sold; the whole profit is simply what the customer paid less what the tanker cost. Each side settles on its own: either can be cash, a bank account, or on account.

Margin will be calculated automatically

Sales Return / Testing

A customer return is refunded and moves money - fuel comes back into a tank and cash/bank/credit goes back out to the customer. Nozzle testing never involves a customer at all: it drains into the same tank and moves no money, it's simply carved out of that nozzle's sale.

Refund amount will be calculated automatically

Loan / Advance / Owner Drawing

A loan/advance to an employee increases what they owe the pump - the usual advance-recovered-later flow. An owner drawing is money the owner personally takes out of the business for their own use - tracked the same way, as a running balance on an "owner" account, but never treated as revenue lost or as a business expense.

Salary Payment Owner

Enter the full salary earned, and optionally how much of it to hold back against an advance the employee already owes. Only the net is actually paid out.

Net paid will be calculated automatically

Cash Handover - Shift Reconciliation

Enter the cash actually counted at the end of each shift. Expected cash is that shift's nozzle sales minus credit given minus bank sales. This is a check, not a transaction - it never changes any balance by itself, exactly like a tank dip. If a shortfall is real, an owner can write it off as a cash expense from the row below.

Dip - Tank Stock Check

Enter each tank's physical dip reading. Book stock is calculated from starting stock plus purchases minus sales. A small variance is normal (evaporation, temperature, rounding) - it's not treated as an error. Tanks with a calibration chart set up in Settings take a depth in cm (what a dip stick actually measures) and convert to liters automatically; the rest take liters directly.

Net Cash Flow = sales - credit given + receipts - expenses - cash-paid purchases - supplier payments - salaries paid - cash-refunded sales returns + cash-method non-fuel sales - cash-paid product purchases + cash-method other income. Purchases made on supplier credit aren't subtracted at the time of purchase since that cash hasn't left yet - it's counted when the supplier is actually paid; a sales return (or non-fuel sale, or product purchase, or other income) settled via a bank or a customer's/supplier's account is excluded here the same way, since it doesn't move cash-in-hand (see that bank's balance, or the account's balance, instead). For a period profit view (revenue against the cost of fuel and products actually sold), see the Monthly Report.

Delete only works for a tank with no purchases, sales, or dip readings yet - a genuine setup mistake, not real history.

"Stock as of" is the point the starting stock was measured from - every historical stock and dip-variance figure for that tank is reconstructed relative to it (nothing is stored per-date, so changing it just recalculates). Leaving it blank treats the starting stock as if it's always applied, from the beginning.

"Cost/L" is what the starting stock cost to buy - folded into the fuel's weighted average cost the same way a real purchase is, so that stock isn't sold at a zero cost basis. "unknown" for a tank whose historical cost was never recorded (every tank created before this field existed) - leave the field blank on Save to keep it that way; only a typed number changes it.

Products

Lubricants, filters and shop items - counted in whole units or by the litre, never through a nozzle. Editing a rate here records dated history (see product_rates_on_date), so past sales keep costing at the rate that actually applied then. Deactivate rather than delete once a product has sale or purchase history.

Purchase (cost) rate only. Selling price is set on the Inventory page.

Delete only works for a product with no sale or purchase history yet - deactivate it instead once it has some; a deactivated product disappears from future sale pickers but its history and past figures stay intact.

Add a Product

Import Products

Paste a price list here - one product per line, fields separated by commas or tabs (so pasting straight out of a spreadsheet works, same as the dip chart paste below). Column order: name, pack size, purchase rate, retail rate, opening stock, low-stock alert - the last two are optional; when a line omits them, a NEW product gets 0. Use - or leave pack size blank when there isn't one. Category and unit below apply to the WHOLE pasted batch, so paste lubricants together, then filters, separately. Re-pasting the same names later with new rates UPDATES them (keeping full rate history) instead of creating duplicates - matching is by name, case-insensitive. Nothing is imported if any line has an error.

For a product that ALREADY EXISTS, an import updates only its rates, pack size, category and unit - plus the low-stock alert, but only on a line that actually supplies one; leaving that 6th column blank keeps whatever threshold is already set (e.g. from the single-row form above) instead of resetting it to 0. Opening stock for an existing product is never touched by an import - to adjust stock, record a purchase or edit the product directly.

Example - two lines, tab or comma separated:
HELIX H3, 3 L, 3246, 3590, 40, 10
OIL FILTER - COROLLA, -, 350, 500

A price is a historical fact with a date, not one current number - each entry is billed at whichever price was in effect on its own date. So when backfilling older records, set that period's price here first (e.g. "Rs 402.10 from 1 May"), then enter those days. Setting a past price does not disturb today's price; the most recent one still applies now.

If a date has no price recorded on or before it, entries for that date fall back to today's price - which is why the Ledger warns you when that's the case. Each entry stores its own price at the moment it's saved, so correcting a price later will not repair entries already made; use the re-pricing tool below for those.

Re-price Past Entries Owner

Corrected a price after already entering some days? Those entries kept the price they were saved at - this recalculates them against the corrected price history, for a whole date range at once, instead of re-saving each day on the Ledger by hand.

You'll see exactly what would change - every entry's old and new amount, side by side - and nothing is written until you confirm on that screen. Litres are never altered, only the price and the money that follows from it. Credit entries recorded as a deliberate discount ("By Amount") are left alone.

Tank Dip Charts

A dip stick measures depth, not volume. Paste the tank's calibration table here - one depth_cm,liters pair per line (commas or tabs both work, so you can paste straight from a spreadsheet) - and the Ledger will collect dips in cm and convert automatically, interpolating between the points you give. Direct Sale from Tanker Owner

Fuel bought from a supplier and sent straight to a customer - it never enters this pump's tanks and never goes through a nozzle. Nothing here touches tank stock or litres sold; the whole profit is simply what the customer paid less what the tanker cost. Each side settles on its own: either can be cash, a bank account, or on account.

Sales Return / Testing

A customer return is refunded and moves money - fuel comes back into a tank and cash/bank/credit goes back out to the customer. Nozzle testing never involves a customer at all: it drains into the same tank and moves no money, it's simply carved out of that nozzle's sale.
